MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  JUNE 10, 2024
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  6:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Uhring called the meeting to order at 5 :00 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Steve Uhring; Mayor Pro Tem Doug Stewart; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Bruce Silverstein

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION

  Mayor Uhring opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: None.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

  At 5:00 p.m., the Council recessed to Closed Session to discuss the following items listed
  on the Closed Session agenda:

Personnel Matters pursuant to Government Code Section 54957:

  1.  Public Employee Performance Evaluation
  Title: City Manager

Conference with Real Property Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.8

  1.  Property Known as The Malibu Lumber Yard (3 939 Cross Creek Road APN
  4458-020-903)
  City Negotiator: City Manager Steve McClary or his Designee.
  Negotiating Parties: WPG Malibu LLC, AJS Lumberyard LLC, 9308 Civic
  Center Drive LLC
  Under Negotiation: Price and Terms

Conference with Legal Counsel — Existing litigation pursuant to Government Code Section
54956.9(d)(1):

  l.  Case Name: City’s Petition to Form Malibu USD from Territory in the Santa
  Monica-Malibu USD

  Minutes of June 10, 2024

  REGULAR SESSION CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Uhring called the meeting to order at 6:46 pm.

  ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Steve Uhring; Mayor Pro Tem Doug Stewart; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Bruce Silverstein

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Steve McClary, City Manager;
  Joseph Toney, Assistant City Manager; Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey
  Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Yolanda Bundy,
  Environmental Sustainability Director; Richard Mollica, Flaming Director; Susan Dueflas,
  Public Safety Director; Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director; Parker Davis, Media
  Technician; Christina Munoz, Deputy City Clerk; Chris Orosz; Recreation Supervisor;
  Solishia Andico, Environmental Sustainability Analyst; Mark Johnson, Environmental
  Programs Coordinator; and Brandie Ayala, Administrative Analyst

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Interim City Attorney Rusin reported that the meeting convened at 5:00 p.m., after which
  time the City Council recessed to a Closed Session pursuant to Government Code Sections
  54957, 54956.8, and 54956.9, with all Councilmembers present. He stated the Council
  discussed the items on the Closed Session agenda and took no reportable action.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Graeme Clifford led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettij ohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on June
  1, 2024, with the amended agenda posted on June 7, 2024.

  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

  MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a motion
  t0 approve the agenda. The motion carried unanimously.

  ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS
l
  None.

  ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 10, 2024
  Page 3 of 15

Time Pera, Mountains Recreation Conservation Authority (MRCA) Ranger,
provided the Ranger activity report for the last month. He stated 240 parking
citations were issued, two service calls were generated, and one rescue was initiated
at the Escondido Trail due to a sprained ankle. He stated extended ranger patrols
and maintenance division shifts were scheduled during Memorial Day weekend.
He stated Rangers responded to a report of a possible homeless encampment at
Malibu Bluffs. He stated 10 administrative citations were issued at Lechuza Beach
and Escondido Canyon Trail for dogs on the beach, illegal off-trail use, smoking,
and the possession of alcohol. He announced Los Angeles County Public Works
had commenced road repairs along Murphy Way and would begin road repairs
along Winding Way next Monday. He stated the project effected access to
Escondido Park and from June 17-20, 2024 and June 25-27, 2024 MRCA would
direct the public to access the park using Via Escondido.

In response to Councilmember Grisanti, Ranger Pera stated he did not know if the
City issued a permit for the road work. He stated the work was being performed
by Caltrans or Los Angeles County Public Works;

Mayor Pro Tem Stewart stated there was ongoing litigation regarding the easement
over Via Escondido. He stated these were private roads and the road construction
was not being performed by the City.

Is response to Mayor Uhring, Ranger Pera stated he would clarify what notice was
being provided to residents on Via Escondido.

In response to Interim City Attorney Rusin, Ranger Pera stated he did not know
how parking would be managed on Via Escondido.

In response to Councilmember Riggins, Ranger Pera stated it was expected that
visitors would access Via Escondido on foot from PCH. He stated the extended
ranger patrols were for the three days of Memorial Day weekend and the parking
lot was closed at one point to protect public safety. He stated two additional rangers
were scheduled, four total, for the weekend. He stated additional maintenance team
staffing was also scheduled.

Councilmember Silverstein thanked Ranger Pera for his update and stated his
supervisors should explain the plan for Via Escondido.

Mayor Pro Tem Stewart stated Via Escondido had once been identified as the
Haunted House Trail, but that designation had been corrected and the easement was
subject to litigation.

Jo Drummond announced the monthly hand weeding event at Point Dume
Headlands this Wednesday. She discussed Mayor Pro Tem Stewart’s comments on
decorum when discussing the May l3, 2024 Regular meeting. She discussed the
comments directed to her as the appellant for the Malibu Inn Motel project. She
discussed the comments and questions directed to the staff member presenting the
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 10, 2024
  Page 4 of 15

  report.

  Graeme Clifford requested Commissioners be allowed to participate in
  Commission meetings Virtually.

  Mario Sandoval read a letter from Elena Eger into the record.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Mr. Sandoval stated the January 5, 2024
  letter from the California Coastal Commission was attached to the MRCA’s
  February l2, 2024 correspondence.

  Ryan Embree discussed Ranger Pera’s comments. He stated beach access signs
  should be placed by the California Coastal Commission, not the City. He discussed
  the May 13, 2024 hearing for the Malibu Inn Motel proj ect. He discussed the joint
  Public Safety Commission and Public Works Commission meeting and requested
  these types of meeting be recorded in the future.

  Bill Sampson discussed Mr. Sandoval’s comments. He discussed how MRCA’s
  beach accessway was open all night. He discussed the location of the beach
  accessway signs MRCA placed last year.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  Jo Drummond discussed the joint Public Works Commission and Public Safety
  Commission meeting last Wednesday to discuss PCH projects and provided an
  update on those projects. She announced a meeting on June 26, 2024 for the
  Caltrans Master Plan for PCH.

  Mayor Uhring stated recording the joint meeting would be beneficial for public
  awareness.

  City Manager McClary stated staff planned to record the next joint Public Works
  Commission and Public Safety Commission meeting. He stated the temporary day-
  use impound yard at Malibu High School (MHS) had started operations on May 25,
  2024. He stated over 50 vehicles had been towed, and the yard would continue to
  be used on weekends and holidays through September 2, 2024. He stated staff
  continued to monitor SB 1297 and AB 1509. He announced City Hall would be
  closed for Juneteenth on June 19, 2024. He stated three additional community land
  outreach events had been held and the next event would be held on June 13, 2024
  at Malibu West Beach Club. He stated the community land outreach survey would
  open on June 17, 2024. He stated he participated in a school district separation
  mediation meeting and a Las Virgenes-Malibu Council of Governments (COG)
  technical advisory committee meeting. He reported the live fuel moisture level was
  good and encouraged the public to prepare for fire season.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, reported crime
  statistics from May 2024. He stated there were 31 Part One crimes in May and 158
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 10, 2024
  Page 5 of 15

  total Part One crimes this year. He stated 25 of the Part One crimes were related t0
  burglary 0r theft. He discussed a traffic stop on May 19, 2024 Where narcotic
  paraphernalia and an unpermitted firearm were found. He discussed a break-in
  attempt on June 8, 2024. He discussed the arrest of three individuals for theft of
  gasoline from a gas station. He discussed a joint pursuit with California Highway
  Patrol (CHP) and the Sheriffs Department.

ITEM 2.C.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Grisanti stated he attended a school district separation mediation
  meeting on June 4, 2024. He stated he attended the Malibu Little League closing
  ceremony. He stated he attended a Public Safety Fair in Calabasas with other
  elected officials and he recommended the public remove brush on their properties
  before fire season.

  In response to Councilmember Riggins, Ms. Drummond stated the Malibu
  Township Council meets once a month. She stated anyone interested in joining the
  group could email her or email info@malibutownshipcouncil.org.
  In response to Councilmember Riggins, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated staff
  could not refuse a complete permit application. He stated if the application was for
  a project legally entitled to a hearing before the Flaming Commission or City
  Council it would need to be brought to a hearing and could not be denied by staff.

  Councilmember Riggins stated she attended a school district separation mediation
  meeting and the Malibu Little League closing ceremony. She expressed concern
  some members of the public would not be able to attend the next community land
  meeting because it was scheduled for mid-morning.

  Councilmember Silverstein discussed statements from the public that certain
  applications should be refused and stated he believed they meant that staff should
  recommend denial on more applications. He discussed Lonnie Gordon’s Malibu
  Times letter to the editor in response to Mayor Pro Tem Stewart’s letter to the editor
  regarding meeting decorum. He discussed specific comments in Mayor Pro Tem
  Stewart’s letter to the editor and stated he did not believe staff had been verbally
  abused at the May 13, 2024 meeting. He stated a Sheriffs Deputy was always
  present at City Council meetings. He stated a staff member had requested a copy
  of one of the emails Councilmember Silverstein referenced in his own comments
  at the May 13, 2024 meeting and that email was included in the staff report for the
  item. He stated he watched the Planning Commission meeting where the cell tower
  at Santa Monical College was discussed. He discussed the FPPC complaint from
  Ann Ravel and stated the FPPC had determined to investigate the complaint.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart stated he attended the community lands outreach meeting
  on May 29, 2024 and an Administration and Finance Subcommittee meeting. He
  stated he was disappointed MRCA had sent Ranger Pera as a messenger and he
  hoped other representatives from MRCA would participate in the future. He
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 10, 2024
  Page 6 of 15

thanked Ranger Pera for his work.

In response to Mayor Pro Tem Stewart, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated AB 361 ,
which allowed for remote meetings under the Brown Act, had expired. He stated
staff would bring back an item on hybrid meetings.

Mayor Pro Tem Stewart addressed Mr. Embree and stated the city’s recording
secretaries would make audio recordings of Commission meetings for the purpose
of finalizing minutes. He stated the beach accessway signs placed by the MRCA
last summer were on inappropriate posts and presented a safety hazard. He
discussed his letter to the editor in The Malibu Times and what he observed
between staff and the public during the meeting. He discussed the City Council’s
Rules of Procedure and Decorum and the importance of proper decorum. He
requested staff consider adding the decorum standards to the Request to Address
the City Council form.

Mayor Uhring encouraged the public to complete their brush clearance. He
discussed the appeal items in the Malibu Inn Motel appeal. He stated the City’s
press release on airplane noise had been well received. He requested a meeting
with the Sheriffs Department to discuss traffic noise enforcement. He stated he
had heard concerns from the public about Nobu.

In response to Mayor Uhring, City Manager McClary stated staff was considering
making a change on staff recommendations for variances to take a more neutral
tone.

In response to Mayor Uhring, Planning Director Mollica stated staff would bring
back an ordinance to accept the California Coastal Commission changes to the
City’s LCPA for wireless communication facilities. He stated staff was available
to meet with any interested parties.

Mayor Uhring discussed code enforcement and the large volume of open cases. He
stated life, health, and safety matters needed to be addressed quickly.

In response to Mayor Uhring, City Manager McClary stated the statistics
represented all cases which had not been closed and staff respOnds to health and
safety concerns immediately. He stated approximately half of the open cases were
for construction without a permit and it takes time to work through the correction.

Councilmember Riggins stated health and safety violations can also be replacement
of septic systems or unpermitted work which needed to work through a Planning
process.
Mayor Pro Tem Stewart stated he would like to see more information on the open
code enforcement cases. He stated the City had purchased sound meters for the
Sheriff’s Department that could be used for traffic noise enforcement.
